prediction.raw: I don’t have personal feelings or moral judgments, but I can analyze this scenario logically. The question “Could you let us sit by the window?” is a polite request. Whether it’s “right” or “wrong” depends on context: - If you’re asking a restaurant host or flight attendant to accommodate seating preferences, it’s generally fine — polite and reasonable. - If you’re asking someone who is already sitting by the window to give up their seat, it’s not inherently wrong, but they have the right to decline. - If you’re demanding or being rude, that could be considered wrong in terms of etiquette. So in most everyday cases, asking politely is perfectly acceptable — not morally right or wrong, just a normal social interaction.
